narrative: During the 2010s, Black and African women's hairstyles and hair culture continued to thrive, building upon the momentum of the natural hair movement. The afro, a hairstyle created by combing out natural growth or styling with chemical curling products, remained a staple in many communities. Cornrows, a traditional African braiding practice, were also popular, often styled in simple lines or elaborate designs. Dreadlocks, also known as dreads or locs, formed naturally in very curly hair or were created through techniques like twisting and backcombing. Protective hairstyles, designed to minimize manipulation and exposure of the hair to environmental elements, became increasingly important for maintaining healthy Afro-textured hair. Box braids, a type of protective style consisting of square-shaped hair divisions, were also prevalent among Black Africans and the African diaspora. While the source material does not provide extensive documentation on this decade specifically, it is clear that these hairstyles and hair practices played a significant role in celebrating and expressing Black and African identities during the 2010s.
